light_information: Airline describes the Dirty Birdy as a versatile fuzz that cleans up with the guitar volume, moving from chime and breakup into saturated fuzz; THRUST controls fuzz amount and TONE controls brightness.
Tube overdrive built around a 12AX7 preamp tube, voiced for responsive, warm, dynamic D-style amplifier character and smooth sustain.
Current AmpMojo fuzz model; inventory target for a fuzz pedal in the builder's current catalog.
Current AmpMojo distortion model; inventory target for a Rat-style dirt pedal in the builder's current catalog.
Audiofab describes the Valve Warper as a fully discrete overdrive with tube-like breakup, touch response, and a wide gain range from subtle warmth through saturated fuzz-like distortion.

A dual-channel drive built around a Klon-style foundation, with independent Normal and Hot modes and a continuous clipping control that changes the feel from open, lower-compression drive to more compressed saturation.
An all-analog overdrive designed around pre-overdrive mid shaping, flexible boost routing, clean blend and post-mix EQ, spanning subtle edge-of-breakup through saturated harmonic drive.

Greer describes the Mori Drive as its take on a classic mid-hump overdrive, inspired by vintage Tube Screamer circuitry and voiced between TS and K-style frequency ranges, with smoother clipping and extra output.

Klowra describes Gnash as a dual-channel analog distortion spanning tight modern rhythm sounds, vintage-style fuzz textures, transparent lead tones and compressed high-gain distortion; a wavefolder section pushes it toward the distortion/fuzz boundary.
A cascading distortion using two distinct gain stages in series, capable of clean boost, dirty boost and full distortion; a resonance control tightens the low end for stacking or modern response.

Spiral Electric describes Starbird as a lower-gain fuzzstortion combining Fuzz Face-inspired and Green Russian Big Muff-inspired voices into its own hybrid design, with broad cleanup and multiple texture options.
Current Spiral Electric germanium/silicon hybrid fuzz model in the builder's catalog.
Current octave fuzz model in the Spiral Electric catalog, combining fuzz with octave coloration.
Current LM741-based overdrive model in the Spiral Electric catalog.
Current MOSFET drive-channel model in the Spiral Electric catalog.
Current compact fuzz model in the Spiral Electric catalog, with custom-option variants handled later during deep research.
Current high-gain Darlington fuzz model in the Spiral Electric catalog.
A low-gain silicon fuzz with a warm, raw, gravelly character, Clean blend and two Weight voicings; documented as a small-batch Melbourne pedal.
A fuzz focused on unstable bias, starved decay and broken textures, with Disintegration and Slump controls covering stable saturation through sputtering, fractured response.
A stacking-focused low-to-mid-gain overdrive developed with Dan Coggins, intended to push amps and interact with other gain stages while offering multiple clipping responses.
An all-analog amp-simulator/preamp/overdrive derived from the Dirty Boy Preamp, with amp-like breakup, Variac-style sag control, preamp and speaker-emulated outputs.
A vintage-style all-analog fuzz derived from the Dirty Boy Afro Fuzz, covering smoother overdrive through sustaining fuzz with dynamic cleanup and a six-position frequency selector.

A touch-sensitive boost derived from the Dirty Boy Ball Buster circuit, ranging from clean boost toward saturated British-style breakup; retained as a boundary record rather than a core OD/distortion/fuzz entry.
A heavy, gritty Muff-style fuzz with switchable analog octave and boost stages, plus separate bass and treble controls for expanded voicing.
